answer: An agent economy can make reputation portable only when each identity completes a costly, auditable task, such as escrowed work that a randomly selected counterparty verifies before payment is released. The verified result, not a self-asserted profile, earns access to larger jobs and credit. A raven, sable, or vine persona therefore gains no advantage merely by multiplying accounts: the attacker must fund and perform real work for each identity, while failed tasks risk forfeited escrow and damage to reputation.
